cards.explanation: The answer is thirteen years, friends! The text says Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, "…took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace." (1 Kings 7:1). That's a long time to wait on one building. I once waited on a batch that long in my head, and it was only forty minutes.

The answer is Tyre! "Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre." (1 Kings 7:13). Solomon is Israel's king, and he sends away for a craftsman. When you need the right person for the job, you go get the right person.

The answer is bronze! Huram "…had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work." (1 Kings 7:14). Every KIND of bronze work. Not some. Every. I can stamp cookies and that's about my whole résumé.

The answer is True! Huram "…was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze." (1 Kings 7:14). So the bronze work runs in the family. Like father, like son.

The answer is False. Huram "…came to King Solomon and carried out all his work." (1 Kings 7:14). Then "…Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD…" (1 Kings 7:40). He finished what he started, friends. That's the kind of worker every boss prays for.

The answer is in the plain of the Jordan! "The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan." (1 Kings 7:46). That's a lot of molten bronze being poured out on that plain. I get nervous with a hot cookie sheet. So I tip my hat to them.

The answer is that there were so many of them! "Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined." (1 Kings 7:47). So many pieces that the weighing never happened. I can't even leave a cookie box unweighed without peeking. So that's a lot of bronze.

The answer is his father David! Solomon "…brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings…" (1 Kings 7:51). David, Israel's former king, set those things apart, and Solomon, his son, carried them in. So David's gifts ended up in the house of the LORD.
The answer is treasuries! Solomon "…placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD." (1 Kings 7:51). That's where David's silver, gold and furnishings went. Good work, bakers!
